messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: routing-policy anomalies detected (high error rate) for smart-routing service. Alert: 3 distinct customers reporting function-calling failures and increased 500s. Start investigating. (alert_id=RTE-20260315-019)
oncall-sre: I'm on it. starting with router logs and policy engine traces. can someone paste the affected tenants?
Priya Patel: Customers A, B, C flagged via Support hooks. seeing spikes at ~02:10 UTC. Support thread id: SUP-8921
Sam Ortiz: grabbing latest router trace. there's a weird loop: requests from eu-west route -> fallback to us-east -> routed back to eu-west due to capacity policy, repeat. looks like fallback decision never marks final state -> causes repeated retries and different model variant selection each hop.
Jae Kim: attaching snippet from router log: 
```
[2026-03-15T02:09:58Z] request id=0f3a route=eu-west target=variant:gptx-3b-quant fallback=enabled
[2026-03-15T02:09:59Z] decision: model_compatibility=true -> send to gptx-3b-quant
[2026-03-15T02:09:59Z] model error: tool_calling not implemented -> 501
[2026-03-15T02:09:59Z] retry trigger: fallback -> region=us-east variant=gptx-3b-fp16
[2026-03-15T02:10:00Z] decision: compatibility_check() returned false for fp16? -> route back to eu-west
```
Marta Ruiz: that log shows the core issue: compatibility_check is returning inconsistent results between nodes. quantized variant is being reported as supporting `tool_calling` by the model registry in some caches.
Theo Zhang: yep, seems like stale compatibility metadata in the cache layer (registry-cache) — some cache shards have old entries marking `gptx-3b-quant` as having `features: [tool_calling]`. new model onboarding removed that.
oncall-sre: immediate mitigation options?
Priya Patel: two-prong approach: 1) disable cross-region fallback policy for affected route (eu-west -> us-east) to stop loops; 2) pin affected tenants to a verified variant (gptx-3b-fp16) until registry caches are reconciled.
Sam Ortiz: doing step 1 now: 
```
# temporarily disable region fallback for smart-routing
rwctl routing update --route smart-default --fallback-regions ""
```
Sam Ortiz: applied. will monitor for removal of retry storms.
oncall-sre: Priya, can you pin customers A/B/C?
Priya Patel: pinning to `gptx-3b-fp16` for customers A,B,C: 
```
rwctl tenancy set-variant --tenant A --variant gptx-3b-fp16 --ttl 2h
rwctl tenancy set-variant --tenant B --variant gptx-3b-fp16 --ttl 2h
rwctl tenancy set-variant --tenant C --variant gptx-3b-fp16 --ttl 2h
```
Priya Patel: pins applied. Support notified customers via support-bot.
support-bot: Support update sent to customers A,B,C: "We are investigating increased errors for function-calling. We've pinned your traffic to a verified model variant while we fix a routing metadata issue. No action needed on your side." :email:
Jae Kim: root cause hypothesis: model-registry cache shards not invalidating feature flags after model onboarding rollback earlier today. some shards returned stale `features.tool_calling=true` for quantized variants. that leads policy engine to think quantized variant supports tool-calling and pass requests; model throws unsupported op -> error -> fallback -> loop.
Theo Zhang: reproducer on staging: forced stale cache entry -> triggers same fallback loop. patch is straightforward: add strict compatibility verification at routing decision time (double-check registry canonical store if cache mismatch) and add telemetry flag for any mismatch.
oncall-sre: can we hotfix in prod quickly? risk of touching policy engine is medium. prefer rate-limited deploy + feature flag.
Sam Ortiz: drafting hotfix: verify compatibility by calling `registry.get_canonical(variant_id)` when `cache.features` disagrees with decision, and if mismatch, treat as incompatible. patch snippet: 
```
if cache.features.tool_calling != canonical.features.tool_calling:
    log.warn("compat-mismatch", variant=variant_id)
    compatibility=false
```
Sam Ortiz: starting canary deploy to router pool #3 (10% traffic) now.
Priya Patel: support tracker: customers A/B/C had ~8-12% of their requests failing for function-calls during the spike window. overall service impact: ~2% error increase across eu-west during 02:08-02:12 UTC.
Marta Ruiz: also checking model build metadata: quantized build was never intended to support tool-calling due to missing custom ops. okay to mark as unsupported permanently. planning to update model catalog entry.
oncall-sre: can we invalidate registry-cache entries globally? Theo?
Theo Zhang: yes, running invalidation across cache-shards: 
```
registryctl cache invalidate --pattern "gptx-3b-quant*" --shards all
```
Theo Zhang: invalidation done at 02:20 UTC. monitoring.
Jae Kim: can confirm router traces now show compatibility_check=false for quant variant and no more retry loops.
Sam Ortiz: canary looked good, promoting hotfix to remaining router pools. deploying to 90% now.
Priya Patel: handoff note for next oncall (Jae will take final verification): ensure registry-cache invalidation fully propagated and remove tenant pins after 2h TTL if telemetry stable.
oncall-sre: escalating to postmortem: root cause = stale model-registry cache + missing strict compatibility verification in routing policy + model catalog mismatch. impact = function-calling failures for 3 enterprise tenants + transient retry storms causing increased latency.
support-bot: Status page update: "Investigating -> Mitigated". Customers notified about temporary pinning.
Jae Kim: final checks: telemetry shows error rates back to baseline. no active loops. I'll follow up in postmortem thread with logs and timeline.
Priya Patel: leaving detailed mitigation steps in incident runbook: added step to invalidate registry cache and to check `features.tool_calling` parity. Also added automated alert when decision engine sees >1 compatibility flip within 5s for same request id.
Marta Ruiz: model-catalog change scheduled: mark `gptx-3b-quant` as `tool_calling:false` and add explicit compatibility tags for quant builds.
Theo Zhang: followup action item: increase TTL for canonical registry read during routing decision from 30s -> 5s? (intent: prefer canonical store reads on mismatch). filing Jira: INF-2347.
oncall-sre: handing off to Jae for on-call until 04:00 UTC. thanks everyone. :thumbsup: 
Jae Kim: acknowledged. final message id=1763456999, closing thread for active mitigation. will open postmortem in /postmortems once writeup ready.
